<!-- pr-reviewer: 075a9c6e8d17bdee38b713aac341e423ea257d81 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`: merges at the next cut; the GUI combo needs a hand check).

### What looks good
- Update/Replace are one `ImportTools` command with ordered `Step`s (Add / Change / Remove) applied in order and inverted in reverse, so one import is one undo step. Remove reuses `DeleteTool` (snapshot restores number, body, cutter); Change goes through the same `ToolDef` set that `ChangeTool` uses (number preserved), and tests cover undo and redo.
- Update/Replace run the `ChangeTool` gates (`torch_refusal`, `retype_refusal`, body/cutter fit) at planning, so a refusal applies nothing. A name that belongs to a non-tool refuses.
- Stale: an op using an updated tool reads Stale (pinned in `update_changes_in_place_keeps_identity_and_number_and_stales_ops`, tool_import_modes.rs:83); the tool keeps its entity and number, so posted T-words do not change.
- No silent data loss: Replace refuses the whole import, naming the tool and operation, if an op uses a tool it would remove; the report lists updated/replaced/removed; an empty plan is refused. Add stays the default and its behaviour is unchanged.
- MCP `import_tool_library` and `cam.importTools` take `mode` (schema enum, cam.d.ts, scripting test, new mcp test), so no follow-up issue is needed. Decision file present. The camcraft-mcp skill is untouched, so no PROCESS_VERSION bump is needed.
- No unwrap/expect/panic added; no snapshot PNGs, goldens, process files or dependencies touched.

### Local results (PR merged with upstream/main, clean merge, no conflicts)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app --test tool_import_modes` | 9 passed |
| `--test tool_library` | 13 passed |
| `--test scripting` | 18 passed |
| `--test mcp` | 14 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD crates/ui) | 531 passed, 5 ignored |
| `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. `tool_import_mode` is sticky view state (state.rs); once set to Replace it stays for later imports in the session. It is guarded by the in-use refusal and is one undo step, but resetting to Add after an import would be the safer default.
2. `tool_import.rs` is now about 290 lines, fine. The GUI combo (pages.rs:1809) has no structural assertion, as the body admits. The maintainer should hand-check the combo and the Update/Replace status text.
3. Matching is by name; #898 is the stated future key.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
